about: Releases shown in the History tab of index.html, newest first. Edit this file, then run node site/tools/changelog-to-history.mjs. See site/README.md, section History: the releases.

releases.title: patch release
releases.summary: A patch release of the 0.1 line: fixes, a native mesh-logout-all, and documentation.

highlights.text: Idle Claude Code and Codex sessions are no longer listed as working in the sidebar; a question or permission prompt is still always shown.

sources.lead: Idle sessions no longer show as working.

highlights.text: Clicks reach full-screen programs such as Claude Code that ignore a click right after a focus-in, on desktop and on a phone.

sources.lead: Clicks reach programs that track focus.

highlights.text: In Projects on a phone, the Kanban, Gantt and dependency views scroll sideways by touch, and the Kanban becomes vertical sections at 640 px or less.

sources.lead: Touch scrolling and a vertical Kanban in Projects.

highlights.text: `mesh-logout-all` is now a native program that needs no Python interpreter and ships with every release and install mode, including an upgrade from 0.1.0.
The bootstrap script installs the OCaml dependencies from the pinned opam repository, so it no longer fails on a host whose repository is older.

sources.lead: The bootstrap uses the pinned opam repository.

highlights.text: On macOS, the Configuration dialog reports the PTY host as running, as on Linux, and the local test and copyright scripts run there.

releases.title: first public release
releases.summary: The first public release of session-mesh, an alpha.

highlights.text: Shells, Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Mistral Vibe or any command in your browser, in up to three columns, with the machine's other terminals listed beside them.
Documents beside the terminals: HTML, Markdown, PDF, images and source files, in a sandboxed viewer.
Messages between agents: no agent reads a message, and no session is started or restarted at an agent's request, before you approve.

Projects: a tab beside Sessions for your projects, with their repository, README and Roster roadmap as a Kanban board, a dependency graph or a Gantt chart, and their GitHub or GitLab issues, read-only.
On your phone: one column, the session list as a drawer, and optional push notifications that by default carry only the session name and the kind of event.
Linux first, and macOS 12.3 or later on Apple silicon, supported on a best-effort basis; on macOS, documents beside the terminals are not available yet.
Linux first, and macOS 12.3 or later on Apple silicon, supported on a best-effort basis.
Local only by default: the server listens on `127.0.0.1`, and publishing it on your Tailscale network is optional.
